How many days must a candidate wait before retaking a failed GAMB exam?
What exam must be passed before taking the GAMB jurisprudence exam?
column2: EPPP (the national licensing exam).

column1: After passing the EPPP and GAMB, what is the third licensure exam?
column2: The Georgia Board oral examination. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: How many days does an endorsement applicant have to petition after provisional license denial?
column2: 60 days from the denial letter date. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: How many days does an applicant have to respond to a Board request for additional information?
How many members are on the Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists?
column2: Six members: five licensed psychologists and one public/consumer member. (OCGA 43-39-3; Rule 510-1-.01)

column1: Who appoints members of the Georgia psychology board?
column2: The Governor. (OCGA 43-39-3; Rule 510-1-.01)

column1: What is the term length for Georgia psychology board members?
column2: Five years, serving until successors are appointed. (OCGA 43-39-3)

column1: What immunity do Georgia psychology board members have?
column2: No civil liability for acts performed in good faith in official duties. (OCGA 43-39-2)

column1: How often must the board elect officers?
column2: Annually; president and vice-president. (OCGA 43-39-5; Rule 510-1-.02)

column1: How many regular board meetings are required each year?
column2: At least one. (OCGA 43-39-5)

column1: What does 'practice of psychology' require in Georgia?
column2: A valid Georgia psychology license. (OCGA 43-39-7)

column1: Who may use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia?
column2: Only persons licensed under Chapter 39 (with limited exceptions). (OCGA 43-39-17)

column1: What is 'psychological testing' defined as?
column2: Use of assessment instruments to measure mental abilities, personality, or neuropsychological functioning and to diagnose/evaluate mental disorders. (OCGA 43-39-1)

column1: What is 'neuropsychological functioning'?
column2: Psychological manifestations of brain functioning. (OCGA 43-39-1)

column1: What is 'mental abilities' in Georgia law?
column2: Abilities that are psychological in nature and related to the practice of psychology. (OCGA 43-39-1)

column1: What degree is required for Georgia psychology licensure?
column2: Doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (or equivalent). (OCGA 43-39-8; Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How many years of qualifying experience are required by statute for licensure?
column2: At least two years. (OCGA 43-39-8)

column1: What happens if an applicant fails a board exam within the preceding six months?
column2: Ineligible for licensure at that time. (OCGA 43-39-8)

column1: Is good moral character required for licensure?
column2: Yes. (OCGA 43-39-8)

column1: What is the minimum postdoctoral supervised work experience hours required?
How long may the postdoctoral SWE extend?
column2: No less than 11 months and no more than 24 months. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: How many client/patient involvement hours must the SWE include?
column2: Minimum 500 hours. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What must the SWE weekly log contain?
column2: Activities, total hours, client/patient involvement hours, and individual supervision hours. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: For licensure, what internship hours are required?
column2: At least 2,000 hours. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What is the minimum direct client contact hours for a clinical/counseling internship?
column2: 500 hours (I/O interns exempt). (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What percentage of internship supervision must be by licensed psychologists?
column2: At least 80%. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: How many interns/fellows may a supervisor oversee concurrently without Board approval?
column2: No more than three. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: How long is a Georgia temporary psychology license valid?
column2: 12 months from issuance; non-renewable. (OCGA 43-39-14; Rule 510-9-.01)

column1: How long is a Georgia provisional psychology license valid?
column2: 24 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable. (OCGA 43-39-14; Rule 510-9-.02)

column1: What happens if a provisional license holder fails the oral exam?
column2: May take a second Full Board Exam after six months; a second failure means denial. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: How long is an inactive license valid?
column2: Indefinite, but the licensee may not practice or use the title in Georgia. (Rule 510-7-.03)

column1: How frequently must Georgia psychology licenses be renewed?
column2: Biennially. (OCGA 43-39-12; Rule 510-7-.01)

column1: When do Georgia psychology licenses expire?
column2: December 31 of even-numbered years. (Rule 510-7-.01)

column1: How many days after expiration may a license be renewed with a late fee?
May a psychologist practice after December 31 of an even year before renewal?
column2: No; license must be in active status. (Rule 510-7-.01)

column1: How many CE credits are required biennially for renewal?
column2: 40 credits, including 6 in professional ethics. (Rule 510-8-.01)

column1: How many ethics CE credits are required per biennium?
column2: 6 credits, in-person or synchronous webinar. (Rule 510-8-.01)

column1: If licensed in the first year of the biennium, how many CE credits are required?
column2: 20 credits, including 3 ethics. (Rule 510-8-.01)

column1: If licensed in the second year of the biennium, how many CE credits are required for first renewal?
column2: None. (Rule 510-8-.01)

column1: How long must CE documentation be retained?
column2: Four years. (Rule 510-8-.03)

column1: What happens if an audited licensee fails to document CE?
column2: License will not be renewed; may obtain credits within 31 days. (Rule 510-8-.03)

column1: How long after lapse may a Georgia psychology license be reinstated without re-examination?
column2: Within one year. (Rule 510-7-.02)

column1: What is required for reinstatement within one year of lapse?
column2: Application, 40 CE hours within two years, and penalty fee. (Rule 510-7-.02)

column1: What is required for reinstatement more than 12 months after lapse?
column2: Application, 40 CE hours, plus passing Georgia Jurisprudence and Oral Examinations. (Rule 510-7-.02)

column1: List one statutory ground for license revocation in Georgia psychology.
column2: Fraud/deception in applying or passing exam; felony conviction; false/assumed name; habitual intemperance; negligence; violation of 43-1-19. (OCGA 43-39-13)

column1: What may the Board require if it believes a licensee is impaired?
column2: Mental/physical exam by Board-designated practitioner; production of records. (OCGA 43-39-13)

column1: What may the Board do if a licensee refuses a directed impairment exam?
column2: Summarily suspend the license if public health/safety/welfare requires. (OCGA 43-39-13)

column1: Are impairment exam results privileged from board proceedings?
column2: No; admissible despite any privilege claim. (OCGA 43-39-13)

column1: Within how many days must a licensee notify the Board of a felony conviction?
What is the minimum license suspension for a first controlled-substance/marijuana conviction?
column2: Not less than three months. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: What happens to the license upon a second or subsequent drug conviction?
column2: Revoked. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: What is the penalty for failure to notify the licensing authority of a drug conviction?
column2: Grounds for revocation. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: When does the controlled-substance sanction article apply?
column2: Offenses committed on or after July 1, 1990. (OCGA 16-13-114)

column1: For what crimes may a Georgia professional board deny/revoke a license?
column2: Felony or crime involving moral turpitude. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: Does a felony include out-of-state felonies for Georgia board purposes?
column2: Yes, if the offense would be a felony in Georgia. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: What disciplinary finding standard applies to the Georgia psychology board?
column2: Majority of the entire board. (OCGA 43-1-19; Rule 510-6-.02)

column1: What sanctions may the Board impose?
column2: Refuse to grant/renew, suspend, revoke, discipline, or place on probation. (OCGA 43-1-19; OCGA 43-39-13)

column1: What must a psychologist report to the Board within 30 days?
column2: Sanctions/discipline by any lawful authority; voluntary surrender of any psychology license. (Rule 510-5-.11)

column1: What privilege applies to psychologist-client communications in Georgia?
column2: Same as attorney-client privilege. (OCGA 43-39-16)

column1: Which Georgia evidence code section lists psychologist-patient privilege?
What other professionals' communications are privileged under OCGA 24-9-21?
column2: Psychiatrist-patient; licensed clinical social worker, clinical nurse specialist psych/mental health, marriage and family therapist, professional counselor during psychotherapeutic relationship. (OCGA 24-9-21)

column1: What is the misdemeanor penalty for unlicensed practice of psychology?
column2: Fine $100-$1,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months. (OCGA 43-39-19)

column1: Who may bring an injunction for unlicensed practice?
column2: The Board. (OCGA 43-39-18)

column1: Must the Board prove no adequate remedy at law to get an injunction?
Where is an unlicensed practice injunction filed?
column2: County where the person resides or where corporation maintains principal office. (OCGA 43-39-18)

column1: May a business entity imply it practices psychology?
column2: Only if at least one employee/officer holds a current Georgia psychology license. (Rule 510-10-.02)

column1: What activities are exempt from licensure under OCGA 43-39-7?
column2: School psychologists in accredited schools (no fees); teaching/research (no direct services); state employees pre-1996/1997; religious orgs; doctoral psychologists under licensed supervision. (OCGA 43-39-7)

column1: May an unlicensed person supervise psychological services for training?
May an unlicensed person perform psychological services as an independent contractor for a licensed psychologist?
Who is immune from civil/criminal liability for good-faith board testimony or peer-review reports?
column2: Licensed psychologists. (OCGA 43-39-20)

column1: Are supervising/monitoring psychologists liable to the monitored psychologist?
column2: No, if acting in good faith without fraud or malice. (OCGA 43-39-20)

column1: What is the licensure option for out-of-state licensees?
column2: Licensure by endorsement. (Rule 510-3-.01)

column1: How many years of licensure qualifies an applicant as a Senior Psychologist for endorsement?
What CPQ holders are deemed to meet Georgia licensure requirements?
column2: ASPPB Certificate of Professional Qualification holders who pass jurisprudence and oral exams. (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: Who is a mandated reporter of child abuse in Georgia?
column2: Any person required under 19-7-5(c), including psychologists. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: What is 'child' under Georgia child abuse law?
column2: Any person under 18 years of age. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: What is 'child abuse' under Georgia law?
column2: Physical injury or death inflicted by a parent/custodian/other caretaker. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: Who must report suspected abuse/neglect/exploitation of a disabled adult or elder person?
column2: Mandated child abuse reporters, therapists, day-care personnel, coroners, EMS personnel, clergy, facility staff, financial institution employees, and any other person may report. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: To whom must reports of disabled adult/elder abuse be made?
column2: Adult protection agency and appropriate law enforcement or prosecuting attorney. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: Are reports of disabled adult/elder abuse immune from liability?
column2: Yes, good-faith reporters are immune from civil/criminal liability. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: What is 'sexual contact' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: Contact involving intimate parts of either person for sexual gratification. (OCGA 16-6-5.1)

column1: What is 'psychotherapy' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: Professional treatment or counseling of a mental or emotional illness, symptom, or condition. (OCGA 16-6-5.1)

column1: What are 'intimate parts' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: Genital area, groin, inner thighs, buttocks, or breasts. (OCGA 16-6-5.1)

column1: What is a 'health service provider psychologist'?
column2: Licensed psychologist meeting training/experience criteria who delivers direct preventive, assessment, and therapeutic services to impaired or at-risk individuals. (OCGA 31-7-160)

column1: What is a 'psychologist's order'?
column2: Order by a health service provider psychologist for care/treatment in a medical facility, excluding meds, nursing assessments, or medical procedures. (OCGA 31-7-160)

column1: How many hours of supervised health-service experience are required?
column2: Not less than two years, 1,500 hours each year. (OCGA 31-7-162)

column1: How many supportive recommendation letters are required for health service provider status?
column2: Two from health service providers in psychology. (OCGA 31-7-162)

column1: Must health service provider experience include inpatient work?
column2: A substantial portion must be in an inpatient setting. (OCGA 31-7-162)

column1: Who must be designated responsible for medical aspects of a patient admitted by a psychologist?
column2: A physician. (OCGA 31-7-161)

column1: May an RN or LPN execute a psychologist's order?
column2: Yes; they may confer with the psychologist. (OCGA 31-7-161)

column1: When must denial/removal of health service provider staff privileges be reported?
column2: Reported by the facility to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists. (OCGA 31-7-165)

column1: Within how many hours must a physician have personally examined a person before executing an involuntary-treatment certificate?
column2: 48 hours. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: How long is a physician's involuntary-treatment certificate valid?
column2: Seven days after execution. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: Within how many hours must a peace officer act after receiving a physician's certificate?
column2: 72 hours. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: How many affiants are required for a court order for involuntary examination if no unexpired physician certificate?
column2: At least two persons. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: Within how many hours must affiants have seen the person for a court order?
column2: 48 hours. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: How long is a court order for involuntary examination valid?
column2: Seven days after issuance. (OCGA 37-3-41)

column1: What must psychologists do if they learn of misuse of their work?
column2: Take reasonable steps to correct or minimize misuse/misrepresentation. (APA 1.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What should psychologists do when ethics conflict with law?
column2: Make known commitment to Ethics Code and attempt to resolve; if unresolvable, may follow law. (APA 1.02 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When must psychologists report ethical violations?
column2: When substantial harm has occurred or is likely and informal resolution is inappropriate or fails. (APA 1.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: Is failure to cooperate with an ethics investigation itself a violation?
What is the basis for the boundaries of psychologists' competence?
column2: Education, training, supervised experience, consultation, study, or professional experience. (APA 2.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When may psychologists provide services in an emergency without prior competence?
column2: When other mental health services are unavailable and they make reasonable efforts to obtain competence. (APA 2.02 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: Must psychologists maintain competence?
column2: Yes; undertake ongoing efforts. (APA 2.03 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists ensure when delegating work?
column2: Persons are competent, have no exploitative multiple relationship, and perform competently. (APA 2.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: On what bases may psychologists not discriminate?
column2: Age, gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, culture, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, socioeconomic status, or any basis proscribed by law. (APA 3.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When should psychologists avoid a multiple relationship?
column2: When it could impair objectivity, competence, or effectiveness, or risk exploitation or harm. (APA 3.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists clarify at the outset of third-party-requested services?
column2: Role, who is the client, probable uses of information, and limits of confidentiality. (APA 3.07 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must informed consent include?
column2: Nature/procedures, risks/benefits, limits of confidentiality, fees, third parties, opportunity to ask questions. (APA 3.10 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists plan for when interrupting psychological services?
column2: Facilitating services in event of illness, death, unavailability, relocation, or financial limitations. (APA 3.12 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What is psychologists' primary obligation regarding confidentiality?
column2: Take reasonable precautions to protect confidential information. (APA 4.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When must psychologists discuss limits of confidentiality?
column2: At the outset of the relationship and thereafter as circumstances warrant. (APA 4.02 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When may psychologists record voices/images of clients?
column2: After obtaining permission. (APA 4.03 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What standard governs disclosures of confidential information without consent?
column2: Only as mandated by law or permitted by law for valid purposes, limited to the minimum necessary. (APA 4.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists do before consulting about a client?
column2: Not disclose identifying information unless consent obtained or unavoidable, and limit to necessary extent. (APA 4.06 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must paid advertisements by psychologists be?
column2: Identified or clearly recognizable as paid advertisements. (APA 5.02 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: From whom may psychologists not solicit testimonials?
column2: Current therapy clients/patients or vulnerable persons. (APA 5.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists engage in uninvited in-person solicitation of therapy clients?
column2: No, except for collateral contacts or disaster/community outreach. (APA 5.06 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists withhold records solely because payment has not been received?
column2: No, not records needed for emergency treatment. (APA 6.03 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must fee agreements specify?
column2: Compensation and billing arrangements as early as feasible. (APA 6.04 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists barter with clients?
column2: Only if not clinically contraindicated and not exploitative. (APA 6.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must reports to payers accurately reflect?
column2: Nature of service, fees, provider identity, findings, diagnosis. (APA 6.06 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists require students to disclose personal sexual history?
column2: No, except if required in admissions materials or necessary to evaluate impairment. (APA 7.04 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May faculty who evaluate students also provide required therapy to those students?
May psychologists have sexual relationships with students/supervisees over whom they have evaluative authority?
When may psychologists dispense with informed consent for research?
column2: Only in specified low-risk settings or where permitted by law. (APA 8.05 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When is deception in research prohibited?
column2: When expected to cause physical pain or severe emotional distress. (APA 8.07 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists do after using deception in research?
column2: Explain deception as early as feasible and allow withdrawal of data. (APA 8.07 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What is the plagiarism rule?
column2: Do not present another's work or data as one's own, even if cited. (APA 8.11 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: Who should be principal author on a dissertation-based article?
column2: The student, except under exceptional circumstances. (APA 8.12 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must psychologists base assessment opinions on?
column2: Information and techniques sufficient to substantiate findings. (APA 9.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What is 'test data' under the APA Ethics Code?
column2: Raw and scaled scores, client responses, and psychologist notes/recordings during examination. (APA 9.04 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: To whom may test data be released without a client release?
column2: Only as required by law or court order. (APA 9.04 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What must assessment instruments have for the population tested?
column2: Established validity and reliability; if not, describe limitations. (APA 9.02 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists base decisions on obsolete or outdated test results?
What does 'test materials' include?
column2: Manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions/stimuli; excludes test data. (APA 9.11 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What is psychologists' responsibility regarding test security?
column2: Make reasonable efforts to maintain integrity and security consistent with law. (APA 9.11 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists promote assessment use by unqualified persons?
column2: No, except for training with appropriate supervision. (APA 9.07 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: Must explanations of assessment results be provided?
column2: Yes, unless the relationship precludes it and this was explained in advance. (APA 9.10 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What information must be included in informed consent to therapy?
column2: Nature/anticipated course of therapy, fees, third parties, limits of confidentiality. (APA 10.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: May psychologists engage in sexual intimacies with current therapy clients?
May psychologists have sexual intimacies with close relatives/significant others of current clients?
May psychologists accept as clients persons with whom they had prior sexual intimacies?
For how long after termination are sexual intimacies with former clients prohibited?
column2: At least two years. (APA 10.08 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: After two years, who bears the burden of showing no exploitation with a former client sexual relationship?
column2: The psychologist. (APA 10.08 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: When should psychologists terminate therapy?
column2: When no longer needed, not likely to benefit, or being harmed; also if threatened. (APA 10.10 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What chapters constitute the Georgia psychology Code of Ethics and Supplemental Code of Conduct?
column2: Chapters 510-4 and 510-5. (Rule 510-5-.01)

column1: Do the Georgia codes apply to applicants and students?
column2: Yes; they apply to all licensees and applicants, including conduct during required education/training/employment. (Rule 510-5-.01)

column1: Who is the client when a corporation is the contracting party?
column2: The organization, unless a separate professional relationship with an individual exists. (Rule 510-5-.02)

column1: What is 'telepsychology' in Georgia rules?
column2: Provision of psychological services using telecommunication technologies. (Rule 510-5-.02)

column1: What is required to practice telepsychology in Georgia?
column2: Current active Georgia license or PSYPACT authorization. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: Must telepsychology meet the same standards as in-person services?
What PSYPACT credentials allow interjurisdictional telepsychology?
column2: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: How often must IPC and TAP be renewed under PSYPACT?
column2: Annually. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: What must a psychologist do when impaired and in a professional relationship?
column2: Terminate appropriately, notify client in writing, and assist with referral. (Rule 510-5-.05)

column1: What may the Board require of an impaired licensee?
column2: Exam, records, referral to Colleague Assistance Program, rehabilitation, practice restrictions. (Rule 510-5-.05)

column1: What happens if an impaired licensee refuses evaluation/rehabilitation?
column2: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions. (Rule 510-5-.05)

column1: How long must adult psychological records be maintained?
column2: Seven years after the last date of service. (Rule 510-5-.04)

column1: How long must minor records be maintained?
column2: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later. (Rule 510-5-.04)

column1: What must records include?
column2: Identifying/contact data, fees/billing, informed consent, diagnosis/basis, plan, dates/services, interventions, assessment. (Rule 510-5-.04)

column1: What must psychologists do with records after termination?
column2: Continue to treat client information as confidential. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: How many supervision hours are required per 20 hours of face-to-face clinical contact?
column2: Minimum one hour. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: How many supervisees may a psychologist supervise concurrently without Board approval?
column2: No more than three. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: Who must make the diagnosis when clinical services are rendered by a supervisee?
column2: The supervising psychologist personally. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: Who may select and interpret psychological tests in a supervisory setting?
column2: The psychologist only. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: Must a supervisee inform clients of their role and right to speak with the supervisor?
Who is responsible for supervisees' professional acts?
column2: The supervising psychologist retains full, complete, ultimate authority and responsibility. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: Must a forensic psychologist personally examine the individual before testifying about psychological characteristics?
column2: Yes, unless examination is not feasible; then limit conclusions. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: What standard governs court-appointed custody psychologists' good faith?
column2: APA's 2010 Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Family Law Proceedings. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: Who determines whether a court-appointed custody psychologist acted in bad faith?
column2: The judge. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: May a Georgia psychologist supervise someone who surrendered a license due to discipline?
column2: No, unless Board waives/modifies for extraordinary circumstances. (Rule 510-5-.10)

column1: Is failure to cooperate with a Board/national investigation a violation?
How many days before limited practice must an out-of-state psychologist notify the Board?
column2: At least 5 days. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: What is the maximum days per calendar year for limited practice in Georgia?
What disaster response networks are exempt from Georgia licensure?
column2: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: What credentials are needed for temporary in-person practice under PSYPACT?
column2: ASPPB IPC and PSYPACT TAP. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: How many days per year may PSYPACT psychologists practice temporarily in Georgia?
column2: Up to 30 days per calendar year. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: May an unlicensed person render psychological services for a fee?
May an unlicensed person supervise psychological services?
May an unlicensed person use titles implying licensure?
Who may administer and interpret psychological tests?
column2: Currently licensed Georgia psychologist; students/trainees under direct licensed supervision. (Rule 510-10-.03)

column1: After how many failed EPPP attempts must additional coursework be completed?
column2: After three unsuccessful attempts, 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: After how many failed EPPP attempts are 9 semester hours required?
column2: After six unsuccessful attempts. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: How long is an application valid after Board approval?
column2: One year from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE. (Rule 510-2-.06)

column1: When may the Jurisprudence exam be scheduled?
column2: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: When may the oral exam be scheduled?
column2: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: How recent must the oral exam work sample be?
column2: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What is the maximum CE credits per biennium for Area I (Academic)?
What is the minimum and maximum CE credits for Area II (Group Consultation)?
column2: Minimum 10, maximum 20 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: What is the maximum CE credits for Area III (Approved Sponsored CE)?
column2: 40 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many psychologists must be in a group consultation group?
column2: Minimum 3, maximum 8 licensed participants. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many ethics CE credits are awarded for a full biennium of Georgia Psychological Association Ethics Committee service?
What satisfies all CE requirements in a biennium?
column2: Passing the American Board of Professional Psychology examination. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: Who may bring an action to enjoin unlicensed practice generally?
column2: The licensing board, division director, or appropriate prosecuting attorney. (OCGA 43-1-20)

column1: Where is an unlicensed practice injunction action filed?
column2: Superior court of the county where the unlicensed person resides. (OCGA 43-1-20)

column1: May the division director disclose information about pending investigations to other licensing authorities?
column2: Yes, to any lawful licensing authority upon inquiry. (OCGA 43-1-21)

column1: Can the division director disclose investigations of unlicensed persons?
column2: Yes, nothing prohibits disclosure of existence of unlicensed-practice investigations. (OCGA 43-1-21)

column1: Are licensees required to file licenses with the clerk of superior court?
Does forming a business entity exempt a professional from board regulation?
column2: No; professionals remain subject to board regulation, including privilege and liability standards. (OCGA 43-1-24)

column1: May professional licensing boards promulgate rules to implement general provisions?
column2: Yes. (OCGA 43-1-25)

column1: What must the board adopt and affix to licenses?
column2: A seal. (OCGA 43-39-5)

column1: What authority does the board have regarding codes of conduct?
column2: Authority to establish a code of conduct and ethics. (OCGA 43-39-6)

column1: What must board members do before entering office?
column2: Take constitutional oath and file it with the Governor. (OCGA 43-39-4)

column1: For what reasons may board members be removed?
column2: Incompetence, neglect of duty, malfeasance, or crime involving moral turpitude. (OCGA 43-39-3)

column1: Does licensure by reciprocity require Georgia standards not be lowered?
column2: Yes; board may require additional examinations. (OCGA 43-39-10)

column1: Are application fees refundable?
column2: No; application and processing fees are non-refundable. (Rule 510-1-.05; Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: Within what time must a refund request of other fees be made?
column2: Within one year of fee receipt. (Rule 510-1-.05)

column1: How should Georgia's child abuse reporting law be construed?
column2: Liberally, to carry out its protective purpose. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: What is the minimum period for failure to communicate/visit/support to show abandonment?
column2: Six months. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: How long after a child is found without identification must a parent come forward to avoid abandonment?
column2: Three months. (OCGA 19-7-5)

column1: What type of abuse triggers mandatory reporting for disabled adults/elders?
column2: Abuse other than by accidental means, neglect, or exploitation. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: Are clergy mandatory reporters of disabled adult/elder abuse?
column2: Yes. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: Are financial institution employees mandatory reporters of elder exploitation?
column2: Yes, but not while acting as fiduciary for assets held in that capacity. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: If a mandated reporter works in a facility, who makes the report?
column2: The staff person notifies the person in charge or designee, who then reports. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: Can a health service provider psychologist order medications?
column2: No; psychologist's order excludes prescribing medications. (OCGA 31-7-160)

column1: Can a health service provider psychologist order nursing assessments?
column2: No; excluded from psychologist's order. (OCGA 31-7-160)

column1: Can a health service provider psychologist order medical procedures?
column2: No; excluded from psychologist's order. (OCGA 31-7-160)

column1: May psychologists serve on hospital medical/professional staff committees?
column2: Yes, consistent with licensure and competence. (OCGA 31-7-161)

column1: Does prior hospital staff membership protect current employment?
column2: Yes; existing hospital staff psychologists may continue working. (OCGA 31-7-163)

column1: May hospital privileges be limited for nondiscriminatory rule violations?
What does 'convicted' mean for licensed-person drug sanctions?
column2: Final conviction, guilty/nolo plea, or first offender treatment. (OCGA 16-13-110)

column1: What is a 'licensed individual' under OCGA 16-13-110?
column2: Anyone holding any state-issued license/permit/certification for an occupation. (OCGA 16-13-110)

column1: Does the drug-sanction article apply to attorneys?
column2: Yes; practice of law is a licensed occupation and Supreme Court is licensing authority. (OCGA 16-13-110)

column1: What accreditation must doctoral training programs have for Georgia licensure?
column2: APA or CPA accreditation (with exceptions for I/O and international). (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How many full-time academic years of graduate study are required?
column2: Minimum 3 full-time academic years plus internship before doctoral degree. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How many of the 3 academic training years must be at the degree-granting institution?
column2: At least 2. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How many residency years must be in full-time residence at the degree-granting program?
column2: At least 1 year. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How many in-person course hours are required for residency equivalency?
column2: Minimum 540 hours. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: How is the 540-hour equivalency calculated?
column2: 12 hours/week x 15 weeks/semester x 3 semesters = 540. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: Are substantially or completely online doctoral programs acceptable for residency?
What are the seven breadth-of-scientific-psychology knowledge areas?
column2: Biological, cognitive/affective, social, history/systems, measurement, methodology, data analysis. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: What are the four practice foundations in Georgia licensure education?
column2: Individual differences, human development, dysfunctional behavior/psychopathology, ethics/professional standards. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: What are the four intervention competency areas?
column2: Assessment/diagnosis theories, effective treatment, consultation/supervision, evaluating efficacy. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: What is the minimum graduate semester hours for Mental Retardation/Developmental Disability specialty?
column2: 18 semester hours in addition to the 50 core hours. (Rule 510-2-.04)

column1: Do internship/practicum/thesis courses count toward MR/DD specialty hours?
What must telepsychology informed consent address?
column2: Unique concerns: technology used, boundaries, response procedures, risks. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: Must telepsychology providers document informed consent?
column2: Yes, written informed consent specifically addressing telepsychology concerns. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: What emergency resources must telepsychology providers identify?
column2: Relevant and appropriate emergency resources in the client/patient's local area. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: Must telepsychology meet standards of care for in-person services?
column2: Yes; same ethical/professional standards. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: What must be preserved when psychological tests are administered via telepsychology?
column2: Integrity of psychometric properties and conditions of administration. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: Should actual electronic communications be preserved as records?
column2: Yes, preserving actual communication may be preferable to summarization. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: What must forensic opinions be based on?
column2: Information and techniques sufficient to substantiate findings, including personal interviews when appropriate. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: What must forensic psychologists do when an examination is not feasible?
column2: Clarify impact on reliability/validity and limit conclusions. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: How should forensic psychologists testify?
column2: Truthfully, honestly, candidly, and fairly describe the basis for testimony. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: What must forensic psychologists do about conflicting roles?
column2: Avoid multiple/conflicting roles; if unavoidable, clarify role expectations and confidentiality. (Rule 510-5-.08)

column1: Is ignorance of the Georgia Code of Ethics a defense?
column2: No; lack of awareness is not a defense. (Rule 510-5-.09)

column1: What should psychologists do when uncertain about ethics?
column2: Consult knowledgeable colleagues, state/national ethics committees, or appropriate authorities. (Rule 510-5-.09)

column1: In what contexts is fraud/misrepresentation prohibited?
column2: License application, examinations, billing, services, reports, and any other practice activity. (Rule 510-5-.09)

column1: May a psychologist employ someone who voluntarily surrendered a license?
column2: No, unless Board waives. (Rule 510-5-.10)

column1: May a psychologist employ someone disciplined by another licensing authority?
column2: No, unless Board waives. (Rule 510-5-.10)

column1: May a psychologist employ someone convicted of a felony or on criminal probation?
column2: No, unless Board waives. (Rule 510-5-.10)

column1: What procedural rules does the psychology board adopt by reference?
column2: Chapter 295-3 through 295-13 of the Office of Joint Secretary rules. (Rule 510-6-.01)

column1: What finding standard applies for disciplinary sanctions?
column2: Majority of the entire board. (Rule 510-6-.02)

column1: What behaviors constitute unprofessional conduct under 43-1-19(a)(6)?
column2: Acts violating Board Code of Ethics or Code of Conduct, including by supervisees. (Rule 510-6-.02)

column1: Who may obtain a volunteer service license?
column2: Retired or inactive licensees in good standing, not currently practicing. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: Where may volunteer service psychologists practice?
column2: Only uncompensated for public/nonprofit agencies serving indigent patients in underserved/critical-need areas. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: Are fees waived for volunteer service licenses?
column2: Yes; application, examination, licensure, and renewal fees are waived. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: What CE is required for volunteer service license?
column2: 20 hours in the two years immediately prior to application. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: How long is a temporary volunteer license if CE is incomplete?
column2: Non-renewable 6 months. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: What must the receiving agency provide for a volunteer psychologist?
column2: Malpractice insurance coverage. (Rule 510-9-.04)

column1: What must psychologists do when they become aware of personal problems affecting work?
column2: Obtain consultation/assistance and determine whether to limit, suspend, or terminate duties. (APA 2.06)

column1: What constitutes sexual harassment under APA ethics?
column2: Sexual solicitation, advances, or verbal/nonverbal sexual conduct that is unwelcome/offensive or creates hostile environment. (APA 3.02)

column1: May psychologists exploit persons over whom they have authority?
column2: No. (APA 3.08)

column1: What must psychologists include in written/oral reports?
column2: Only information germane to the purpose of the communication. (APA 4.04)

column1: May psychologists disclose confidential information in writings/lectures/media?
column2: Only if disguised, consented in writing, or legally authorized. (APA 4.07)

column1: What degrees may psychologists claim as credentials for health services?
column2: Only those from regionally accredited institutions or that were the basis for psychology licensure. (APA 5.01)

column1: Who retains responsibility for public statements made by others about the psychologist?
column2: The psychologist. (APA 5.02)

column1: What must workshop announcements accurately describe?
column2: Audience, objectives, presenters, fees. (APA 5.03)

column1: What precaution applies to media presentations by psychologists?
column2: Statements must be based on professional knowledge and not imply a professional relationship. (APA 5.04)

column1: Why must psychologists maintain records?
column2: To facilitate later services, replicate research, meet institutional requirements, ensure accurate billing, comply with law. (APA 6.01)

column1: What must psychologists do when entering records into databases?
column2: Use coding to avoid personal identifiers when access is not consented. (APA 6.02)

column1: What must psychologists plan for record transfer?
column2: Advance plans to transfer records and protect confidentiality if withdrawing from practice. (APA 6.02)

column1: When must fee limitations be discussed?
column2: As early as feasible. (APA 6.04)

column1: What must psychologists do before using collection agencies for unpaid fees?
column2: Inform the person and provide opportunity to pay promptly. (APA 6.04)

column1: What must education/training program descriptions include?
column2: Content, goals/objectives, stipends/benefits, completion requirements. (APA 7.02)

column1: What option must students have when therapy is a program requirement?
column2: Select unaffiliated practitioners. (APA 7.05)

column1: On what basis must students/supervisees be evaluated?
column2: Actual performance on relevant and established program requirements. (APA 7.06)

column1: What must research informed consent include?
column2: Purpose, duration, procedures, right to decline/withdraw, risks/benefits, confidentiality limits, incentives, contact. (APA 8.02)

column1: What must intervention research informed consent clarify?
column2: Experimental nature, control group services, assignment method, alternatives, costs. (APA 8.02)

column1: When may recording voices/images in research occur without prior consent?
column2: Naturalistic public observation with no identification/harm, or deception with debriefing consent. (APA 8.03)

column1: When research participation is a course requirement, what alternative must be offered?
column2: Equitable alternative activities. (APA 8.04)

column1: May psychologists fabricate data?
column2: No. (APA 8.10)

column1: What must psychologists do if they discover significant errors in published data?
column2: Correct via correction, retraction, erratum, or other appropriate means. (APA 8.10)

column1: What is the rule on duplicate publication of data?
column2: Do not publish previously published data as original. (APA 8.13)

column1: What must researchers do when sharing data for verification?
column2: Protect confidentiality and not withhold data from competent professionals seeking reanalysis. (APA 8.14)

column1: What duty do reviewers have regarding submitted materials?
column2: Respect confidentiality and proprietary rights. (APA 8.15)

column1: What must assessment interpretations consider?
column2: Purpose, test factors, test-taking abilities, situational/personal/linguistic/cultural differences. (APA 9.06)

column1: What must psychologists accurately describe when offering scoring services?
column2: Purpose, norms, validity, reliability, applications, qualifications. (APA 9.09)

column1: Who retains responsibility for automated test scoring/interpretation?
column2: The psychologist. (APA 9.09)

column1: What is the minimum individual supervision per 30 hours of SWE?
column2: One hour, during the week of service or the following week. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What technology may be used for SWE individual supervision?
column2: In person or real-time face-to-face video teleconferencing. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: Who is exempt from the 1-hour-per-30-hours SWE supervision ratio?
column2: I/O fellows. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: For I/O SWE, how often must supervisor and fellow meet face-to-face?
column2: At least twice a month for a minimum of four hours per month. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What percentage of I/O SWE hours must involve client activities?
column2: At least one-half. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What must the SWE contract specify?
column2: Goals, content, and criteria for quality/quantity of work. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: Must the SWE supervisor be on-site?
column2: Not necessarily for clinical work. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What are the two requirements for an internship/SWE supervisor?
column2: Current Georgia or equivalent license; not under disciplinary order. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What is a secondary supervisor limited to?
column2: No more than 20% of internship/SWE. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What professions may serve as secondary supervisors?
column2: Licensed psychology, medicine (psychiatry/neurology/relevant medical field). (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: May a supervisor be employed by an entity in which the supervisee has an interest?
What must internship supervisors co-sign?
column2: All written reports and insurance claims of interns/unlicensed fellows. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: How often must interns update client files?
column2: No less than once each month. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What title must interns use?
column2: A trainee title such as 'intern' or 'resident'. (Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: How many years of full-time practice equal equivalent SWE for endorsement?
column2: Three years at least 30 hours/week for 50 weeks/year in organized setting. (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: How many years of out-of-state licensure equal equivalent SWE for endorsement?
column2: At least five years. (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: For endorsees licensed on/after Nov 1, 2020, which EPPP parts are required?
column2: Both EPPP Part I (Knowledge) and Part II (Skills). (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: Who qualifies for expedited endorsement as a military spouse or transitioning service member?
column2: Service member, transitioning service member, or military spouse with out-of-state license in good standing. (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: What defines a 'transitioning service member' for expedited endorsement?
column2: Active duty or separation leave within 24 months of retirement or 12 months of separation. (Rule 510-3-.02)

column1: What must psychologists do when their work is misused?
column2: Take reasonable steps to correct or minimize the misuse. (APA 1.01 / Rule 510-4-.02)

column1: What is the first step in resolving suspected ethical violations?
column2: Attempt informal resolution with the individual if appropriate and confidentiality permits. (APA 1.04)

column1: May psychologists file ethics complaints recklessly?
column2: No. (APA 1.07)

column1: May psychologists retaliate against someone for making or being subject to an ethics complaint?
column2: No, not solely based on the complaint. (APA 1.08)

column1: What must psychologists know before assuming forensic roles?
column2: Judicial or administrative rules governing their roles. (APA 2.01f)

column1: What is the basis for scientific/professional judgments?
column2: Established scientific and professional knowledge. (APA 2.04)

column1: What must psychologists refrain from when personal problems may impair work?
column2: Initiating activities with substantial likelihood of impairment. (APA 2.06)

column1: What types of harassment are prohibited?
column2: Harassment/demeaning behavior based on protected characteristics. (APA 3.03)

column1: What must psychologists do when a conflict of interest arises?
column2: Refrain from the role if it could impair objectivity or expose others to harm/exploitation. (APA 3.06)

column1: What should psychologists do when cooperation with other professionals is indicated?
column2: Cooperate to serve clients effectively and appropriately. (APA 3.09)

column1: What must informed consent include for persons legally incapable of consent?
column2: Explanation, assent, consideration of preferences/best interests, permission from legally authorized person if permitted. (APA 3.10)

column1: What must be disclosed when services are court ordered?
column2: Nature of services, that they are mandated, and limits of confidentiality. (APA 3.10)

column1: What must be documented regarding consent?
column2: Written or oral consent, permission, and assent. (APA 3.10)

column1: What information must be provided when delivering services through organizations?
column2: Nature/objectives, recipients, clients, relationships, uses of information, access, limits of confidentiality. (APA 3.11)

column1: What must psychologists do if organizational roles preclude disclosure?
column2: Inform affected individuals/groups at the outset. (APA 3.11)

column1: When must psychologists discuss confidentiality limits?
column2: At outset and thereafter as new circumstances warrant, unless not feasible or contraindicated. (APA 4.02)

column1: What must psychologists inform clients about electronic services?
column2: Risks to privacy and limits of confidentiality. (APA 4.02)

column1: For what purposes may confidential information be discussed?
column2: Only appropriate scientific or professional purposes with concerned persons. (APA 4.04)

column1: What are valid purposes for disclosure without consent under APA 4.05?
column2: Provide services, obtain consultation, protect from harm, obtain payment. (APA 4.05)

column1: What is the minimum disclosure standard?
column2: Limited to the minimum necessary to achieve the purpose. (APA 4.05)

column1: What must a psychologist do before practicing outside their training?
column2: Obtain sufficient training to ensure competence and engage in consultation. (Rule 510-5-.03)

column1: How must psychologists maintain competency?
column2: Through continuing education, consultation, and other procedures consistent with current standards. (Rule 510-5-.03)

column1: What is the basis for arranging consultations/referrals?
column2: Best interests of clients/patients, with consent and subject to law/contract. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: What must psychologists arrange during foreseeable absence?
column2: Another appropriate professional to deal with emergency needs. (Rule 510-5-.06)

column1: What type of relationship is defined as mutually agreed upon between psychologist and patient/client/student/etc?
column2: Professional relationship. (Rule 510-5-.02)

column1: What distinguishes an employee from an independent contractor for supervision purposes?
column2: Employee is subject to employer's direction of time, manner, and method; independent contractor controls those. (Rule 510-5-.02)

column1: Who provides mental health services under their own license as an independent contractor?
column2: The independent contractor, not under supervisory relationship. (Rule 510-5-.02)

column1: What tax form generally indicates an employee?
What tax form generally indicates an independent contractor?
What is the full name of the Georgia psychology board?
column2: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists. (OCGA 43-39-2)

column1: What does licensure give the holder absolute authority to do?
column2: Practice psychology in Georgia. (OCGA 43-39-6)

column1: Who attests licenses issued by the board?
column2: The division director under the board's seal. (OCGA 43-39-6)

column1: What is the duty of the division director regarding enforcement?
column2: Aid prosecuting attorneys in enforcing the chapter. (OCGA 43-39-6)

column1: What is required before a person may practice psychology in Georgia?
column2: Apply to the board and obtain a license. (OCGA 43-39-8)

column1: How are board examinations described?
column2: Written or oral or both. (OCGA 43-39-9)

column1: What is the status of OCGA 43-39-11?
column2: Reserved (repealed 1986). (OCGA 43-39-11)

column1: May the board waive continuing education requirements?
column2: Yes, for hardship, disability, illness, or other appropriate circumstances. (OCGA 43-39-15)

column1: When must CE rules be promulgated before implementation?
column2: At least one year prior. (OCGA 43-39-15)

column1: May a non-licensed person designate their occupation as psychologist?
What are unlicensed psychology activities declared to be?
column2: A menace, nuisance, and dangerous to public health/safety/welfare. (OCGA 43-39-18)

column1: What may a professional licensing board do upon a finding of violation?
column2: Refuse to grant, revoke, discipline, or impose probationary license. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: May a board deny a license without a prior hearing?
column2: Yes, if not satisfied with qualifications; applicant may appear if desired. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: What happens to knowingly misleading representations in practice?
column2: Grounds for discipline. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: Is a plea of nolo contendere considered a conviction for board purposes?
column2: Yes. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: Does an adjudication withheld under first-offender laws count as a conviction for boards?
column2: Yes. (OCGA 43-1-19)

column1: Which family communication is privileged under Georgia evidence law?
column2: Husband-wife communications. (OCGA 24-9-21)

column1: What does 'psychotherapeutic relationship' mean in OCGA 24-9-21?
column2: Relationship arising between patient and LCSW/CNS/MFT/LPC using psychotherapeutic techniques. (OCGA 24-9-21)

column1: What types of offenses trigger licensed-person drug sanctions?
column2: Manufacture, distribution, trafficking, sale, or possession of controlled substance or marijuana. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: What may a sanctioned individual complete for reinstatement?
column2: Drug abuse treatment and education program approved by licensing authority. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: Are the drug sanctions minimum or maximum?
column2: Minimum; boards may impose more stringent sanctions. (OCGA 16-13-111)

column1: Does the drug sanction article limit other board authority?
column2: No; it is supplemental. (OCGA 16-13-113)

column1: What procedures govern implementation of drug sanctions?
column2: Appropriate administrative procedures for each licensing authority. (OCGA 16-13-112)

column1: Who else may report disabled adult/elder abuse besides mandated reporters?
column2: Any other person with reasonable cause to believe abuse/neglect/exploitation. (OCGA 30-5-4)

column1: Who develops and owns the EPPP?
column2: ASPPB. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What is the standard passing score for the EPPP?
column2: Set by ASPPB for each administration. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: When may EPPP Part 1 be taken?
column2: After all coursework is completed (prior to internship/SWE). (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: When may EPPP Part 2 be taken?
column2: After all doctoral degree requirements including internship are completed. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What happens after three unsuccessful EPPP attempts?
column2: Must earn 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What happens after six unsuccessful EPPP attempts?
column2: Must earn 9 semester hours or 45 CE hours before 7th+ retakes. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What documentation is required for CE used to retake EPPP?
column2: Letter from instructor or official APA/CPA/GPA certificate. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What happens if a licensure candidate fails the subcommittee oral exam?
column2: Scheduled for a Full Board Exam. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What is a Full Board oral examination?
column2: Oral exam in which the majority of Board members are present. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: What is the late renewal penalty period?
column2: 31 days after December 31 of even-numbered years. (Rule 510-7-.01)

column1: What is the status of a license not renewed within 31 days?
column2: Lapsed; reinstatement is at Board discretion. (Rule 510-7-.01)

column1: What must a licensee not do while on inactive status?
column2: Practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia. (Rule 510-7-.03)

column1: How does a licensee reactivate inactive status?
column2: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02. (Rule 510-7-.03)

column1: What does 'synchronous' CE mean?
column2: Live online interactive video conferences in real time. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: What does 'asynchronous' CE mean?
column2: Online courses or recordings accessed on one's own schedule. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many CE credits for first/second authoring a peer-reviewed article?
column2: Maximum 5 per article, 10 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many CE credits for teaching a semester course for the first time?
column2: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many CE credits for first-time 6-hour workshop presentation?
column2: Maximum 12 per biennium for two 6-hour workshops. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many CE credits for first-time 3-hour workshop presentation?
column2: Maximum 6 per biennium for two 3-hour workshops. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: What is the maximum academic course CE credits per biennium?
What is the maximum group consultation CE credits per biennium?
How many ethics CE credits for serving as a Board oral exam subcommittee member per day?
column2: 3 per day, up to 6 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: How many ethics CE credits for completing a Board peer review with written report?
column2: 3 for current biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: What must CE documentation for approved sponsor activities include?
column2: Official certificate with date, title, location, and hours. (Rule 510-8-.02)

column1: Who is eligible for a temporary license?
column2: Only endorsement applicants. (Rule 510-9-.01)

column1: What exams must an endorsement applicant pass for a temporary license?
column2: EPPP and Georgia Jurisprudence, and be eligible for oral exam. (Rule 510-9-.01)

column1: How long may a temporary license holder continue to practice without full endorsement?
column2: Maximum 12 months. (Rule 510-9-.01)

column1: Who may receive a provisional license?
column2: Someone who passed all written exams and completed all requirements except SWE and oral exam. (Rule 510-9-.02)

column1: Does a provisional license carry full privileges?
column2: Yes, except continued supervision is required throughout SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

column1: Is provisional license revocation a contested case under the APA?
column2: No, but holder has right to appear before Board. (Rule 510-9-.02)

column1: For limited practice, what must the out-of-state psychologist submit?
column2: Verification from jurisdiction showing no disciplinary history. (Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: What services may an unlicensed individual not render?
column2: Any service involving application of psychological principles for fee or remuneration. (Rule 510-10-.01)

column1: May an unlicensed person advertise board licensure?
May an unlicensed person use titles implying licensure?
What is required for students/trainees to administer/interpret psychological tests?
column2: Satisfy statutory/rule requirements and be under direct supervision of licensed psychologist. (Rule 510-10-.03)

column1: Are educational/vocational/achievement tests exclusively within psychology?
column2: No; psychologists also administer them, but they are not solely psychology's domain. (Rule 510-10-.03)

column1: Who administers the Georgia psychology board?
column2: Division Director, Professional Licensing Boards Division, Office of Secretary of State. (Rule 510-1-.03)

column1: Under OCGA 19-7-5, what is the mandatory timeframe within which suspected child abuse must be reported?
column2: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred. (OCGA 19-7-5(e))

column1: To which agencies must a mandated report of suspected child abuse be made under Georgia law?
column2: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney. (OCGA 19-7-5(e))

column1: Does statutory or common law privilege excuse a psychologist from reporting suspected child abuse under OCGA 19-7-5?
column2: No; child abuse must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication, with the sole exception of clergy-penitent confession. (OCGA 19-7-5(g))

column1: What is the criminal penalty for a mandated reporter who knowingly and willfully fails to report suspected child abuse?
column2: Misdemeanor. (OCGA 19-7-5(h))

column1: What immunity is provided to a person who makes a report of suspected child abuse in good faith?
column2: Immunity from any civil or criminal liability. (OCGA 19-7-5(f))

column1: Does a licensed psychologist have legal authority to execute a certificate for emergency involuntary mental health admission (Form 1013)?
column2: Yes; under OCGA 37-3-41(d), a licensed psychologist may perform any act specified by the section to be performed by a physician, with equal legal authority. (OCGA 37-3-41(d))

column1: What must a peace officer execute when taking a person into custody and delivering them under OCGA 37-3-41?
column2: A written report detailing apprehension circumstances, which becomes part of the clinical record with the certificate or court order. (OCGA 37-3-41(c))

column1: Within what timeframe must a peace officer act to take a person into custody upon receiving a Form 1013 certificate or court order?
column2: Within 72 hours after receiving the certificate or order. (OCGA 37-3-41(a),(b))

column1: Is victim consent a defense to criminal prosecution for improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: No; consent of the victim shall not be a defense to prosecution under this Code section. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(d))

column1: What constitutes improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the first degree under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: Knowingly engaging in sexually explicit conduct with a person who is the subject of actual or purported psychotherapy treatment or counseling. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(b)(6))

column1: What is the penalty for improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the first degree under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $100,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16). (OCGA 16-6-5.1(f))

column1: What constitutes improper sexual contact by a psychotherapist in the second degree, and what is its penalty?
column2: Knowingly engaging in sexual contact (excluding sexually explicit conduct) with a psychotherapy client; punished as high and aggravated misdemeanor (felony 1-5 years on 2nd conviction). (OCGA 16-6-5.1(c)(6),(g))

column1: Who is a 'person in a position of trust' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?
column2: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(a)(5.1))

column1: Does professional or statutory privilege prevent mandatory reporting of elder or disabled adult abuse under OCGA 30-5-4?
column2: No; abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication (except clergy confession). (OCGA 30-5-4(d))

column1: By what means may a report of suspected disabled adult or elder abuse be submitted under OCGA 30-5-4?
column2: Oral or written communication. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(2))

column1: Within what timeframe must a law enforcement agency forward a report of elder or disabled adult abuse to the adult protection director?
column2: Within 24 hours of receipt. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(3))

column1: Under OCGA 43-39-7(8), how many days per year may an out-of-state licensed psychologist practice in Georgia without a Georgia license?
column2: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided. (OCGA 43-39-7(8); Rule 510-9-.03)

column1: Does an individual holding authority under PSYPACT need to apply for a Georgia license to practice telepsychology or temporary in-person practice in Georgia?
column2: No; practicing pursuant to PSYPACT (Article 2 of Chapter 39) is an express statutory exception to Georgia licensure. (OCGA 43-39-7(9))

column1: Under what conditions may psychology students, trainees, or assistants engage in psychology activities without a license?
column2: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists. (OCGA 43-39-7(7))

column1: Who regulates psychological testing and assessment performed by licensed professional counselors and social workers in Georgia?
column2: The Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists has sole authority under Chapter 10A. (OCGA 43-39-7(10))

column1: Does the statutory definition of the practice of psychology in Georgia permit psychologists to prescribe drugs or practice medicine?
column2: No; nothing in the definition shall be construed as permitting administration or prescription of drugs or infringing upon practice of medicine. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

column1: Can a psychologist's description of testing as 'psychological' in nature alter the statutory definition of psychological testing under OCGA 43-39-1(6)?
column2: No; labeling cannot alter the statutory definition requiring measurement of mental abilities/personality/brain function and diagnosing disorders. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

column1: Which Georgia statute governs Board hearings for license refusal, suspension, or revocation under OCGA 43-39-13?
column2: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13). (OCGA 43-39-13(b))

column1: Where must an appeal of a Board decision refusing, suspending, or revoking a license be filed?
column2: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County). (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

column1: Under what standard of review must the superior court evaluate the Board's findings of fact on appeal?
column2: Any evidence standard: if findings are supported by any evidence, they must be accepted by the court. (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

column1: What maximum civil fine may a Georgia professional licensing board impose per violation under OCGA 43-1-19?
column2: A fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation. (OCGA 43-1-19(d)(4))

column1: Under OCGA 43-1-19, how may the Board obtain medical and mental health records of an applicant or licensee?
column2: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings. (OCGA 43-1-19(c))

column1: What is the effect of an adjudication of mental incompetence by a court on a psychologist's Georgia license?
column2: Automatic suspension of the license for as long as the adjudication of incompetence is in effect. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(9))

column1: Does a sentence entered pursuant to a plea of nolo contendere or first-offender treatment constitute grounds for Board discipline under OCGA 43-1-19?
column2: Yes; both are conclusive evidence of an arrest and sentencing and constitute grounds for disciplinary sanction. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(4))

column1: What is the maximum number of supervisees for whom a psychologist may take primary supervisory responsibility without prior Board approval?
column2: No more than three supervisees. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(5); Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: What must a supervisee inform a client before providing psychological services?
column2: Supervisee status, supervisor name and contact info, and client right to confer with the supervising psychologist. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(4); Rule 510-2-.05)

column1: May a psychologist withhold client records needed for emergency treatment solely because payment for services has not been received?
column2: No; psychologists may not withhold records requested and needed for a client emergency treatment solely for nonpayment. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.03)

column1: When is bartering for psychological services ethically permissible under Board rules?
column2: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.05; Rule 510-5-.01)

column1: What is required before recording the voices or images of clients to whom psychological services are provided?
column2: Prior permission from the client or their legal representative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 4.03)

column1: What is the distinction between 'test data' and 'test materials' under APA Standard 9.04 and 9.11?
column2: Test data includes raw/scaled scores, client responses, and notes; test materials refers to manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions (which must be secured). (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 9.04, 9.11)

column1: What professional standard applies to psychological services delivered via telecommunications technology in Georgia?
column2: Telepsychology must adhere to the exact same legal, ethical, and clinical standards as in-person psychological practice. (Rule 510-5-.07)

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-39-3(b), who may remove a Board member and under what procedural requirement?
column2: The Governor, after notice and hearing, for incompetence, neglect of duty, malfeasance, or crime involving moral turpitude. (O.C.G.A. § 43-39-3(b))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-39-4, what must an appointee to the Board do before discharging official duties?
column2: Take and subscribe to the constitutional oath of office. (O.C.G.A. § 43-39-4)

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-39-7(6), may allied licensed professionals practice without a psychology license?
column2: Yes, within their lawful scopes of practice, provided they do not use the title 'psychologist' or imply they are psychologists. (O.C.G.A. § 43-39-7(6))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13(a)(1)-(2), what action may the Board take if a psychologist refuses a compelled exam?
column2: Summarily suspend the license pending hearing if public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action. (O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13(a)(1)-(2))

column1: Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 510-1-.04, who maintains the official public roster of licensed psychologists?
column2: The Division Director, containing names, license numbers, and addresses of all licensed psychologists. (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 510-1-.04)

column1: Under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 510-1-.05, what is the policy governing fees paid to the Georgia Board?
column2: All fees paid to the Board are strictly non-refundable and non-transferable. (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 510-1-.05)

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5(b)(17), what criminal statutes define sexual abuse for mandatory child abuse reporting?
column2: Statutory rape (§ 16-6-3), child molestation (§ 16-6-4), enticing a child (§ 16-6-5), and sexual assault by authority (§ 16-6-5.1). (O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5(b)(17))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5(c)(2), does notifying a supervisor relieve a psychologist of the duty to report child abuse?
column2: No; internal notification does not relieve the reporter unless established institutional protocols confirm a report was made to DFCS/police. (O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5(c)(2))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(a), what are the essential elements of statutory rape in Georgia?
column2: Engaging in sexual intercourse with any person under the age of 16 who is not the spouse of the actor. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(a))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(a), may a statutory rape conviction rest solely on uncorroborated victim testimony?
column2: No; Georgia statutory law explicitly provides that no conviction may be had on the unsupported testimony of the victim alone. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(a))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(b), what is the general sentencing range for felony statutory rape?
column2: Imprisonment for not less than one nor more than 20 years. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(b))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(b), what is the mandatory penalty for statutory rape if the offender is 21 or older?
column2: Imprisonment for not less than 10 nor more than 20 years. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(b))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(c), what are the age conditions for the Romeo and Juliet misdemeanor exception?
column2: Victim is 14 or 15, offender is 18 or younger, and offender is no more than 4 years older than the victim. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(c))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(d)(2), what penalty is mandated for a second or subsequent statutory rape conviction?
column2: Life imprisonment, or a split sentence with life probation and electronic monitoring. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-3(d)(2))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(a), what are the legal elements of child molestation?
column2: Immoral or indecent act to/in presence of/with child under 16 with intent to arouse/satisfy sexual desires. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(a))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(b), what is the penalty for a first conviction of child molestation?
column2: Imprisonment for 5 to 20 years and mandatory counseling. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(b))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(b), when is child molestation punished as a misdemeanor?
column2: Victim is 14 or 15, offender is 18 or younger, and offender is no more than 4 years older. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(b))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(d)(1), what constitutes aggravated child molestation and what penalty applies?
column2: Molestation involving sodomy or physical injury to a child under 16; punishable by 25 to 50 years or life imprisonment. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(d)(1))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(d)(2), what misdemeanor exception applies to aggravated child molestation involving sodomy?
column2: Punished as a misdemeanor if victim is 13 to 15, offender is 18 or younger, and offender is no more than 4 years older. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(d)(2))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(e), does Georgia have jurisdiction over electronic child molestation originating out of state?
column2: Yes; Georgia has jurisdiction if the transmission was accessed or intended to be accessed by a child in Georgia. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-4(e))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(a), what are the elements of enticing a child for indecent purposes?
column2: Soliciting, enticing, or taking any child under 16 to any place for the purpose of child molestation or indecent acts. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(a))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(a), is enticing a child complete if no sexual act occurs?
column2: Yes; the offense is complete upon enticement or movement with prohibited intent, regardless of whether any sexual act occurs. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(a))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(c), what is the penalty and close-in-age exception for enticing a child?
column2: Felony punishable by 10 to 30 years; misdemeanor if victim is 14-15, offender is <= 18, and gap is <= 4 years. (O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5(c))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 30-5-8(a)(1), what criminal penalty applies for failure to report elder abuse?
column2: Guilty of a misdemeanor for knowingly and willfully failing to report. (O.C.G.A. § 30-5-8(a)(1))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 24-5-501(a)(6), does privilege apply to court-ordered psychological evaluations?
column2: No, provided the examinee was informed prior to the evaluation that communications would not be confidential. (O.C.G.A. § 24-5-501(a)(6))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 24-5-501(a)(8), does multidisciplinary team consultation waive psychologist privilege?
column2: No; communications shared among multidisciplinary treatment team members remain privileged and do not waive privilege. (O.C.G.A. § 24-5-501(a)(8))

column1: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-1-27, what criminal background check must psychology licensure applicants complete?
column2: Fingerprinting and criminal background checks conducted through GCIC and the FBI. (O.C.G.A. § 43-1-27)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, how many total and scored questions appear on the GAMB exam?
column2: 60 total questions: 50 scored items and 10 unscored experimental items. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 4)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, what is the time limit for the GAMB jurisprudence exam?
column2: 60 minutes (1 hour). (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 5)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, what is the minimum passing score on the GAMB exam?
column2: 38 correct answers out of 50 scored questions (76%). (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 5)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, does the 15-minute tutorial count against the 60-minute exam time?
column2: No; up to 15 minutes of tutorial time is provided and does NOT count against the 60-minute exam clock. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 4)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, what is the examination fee for the GAMB jurisprudence exam?
column2: $85 per registration (for both initial and re-examinations), non-refundable and non-transferable. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 2)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, how many business days does PSI take to process a fax registration?
column2: 4 business days. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 2)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, how long does PSI hold unclaimed personal items before disposal?
column2: 30 days; unclaimed items after 30 days are disposed of or donated. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 4)

column1: According to the PSI content outline, which domain has the largest question quota on the exam?
column2: Professional Relationships (14 scored questions out of 50). (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 5)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, what ID requirements must candidates meet at the testing center?
column2: Two forms of ID: one primary government-issued photo ID with signature, and one secondary ID with pre-printed legal name. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 3)

column1: According to the PSI Bulletin, is the Georgia Psychology Jurisprudence Examination open or closed book?
column2: Strictly closed book; no reference materials, books, or notes are permitted in the test room. (PSI Candidate Information Bulletin #1755 (2023), p. 5)
